title: Self-Righteousness
definition: The doctrine of Self-Righteousness teaches that self-righteousness tries to stand before God on personal goodness, religious performance, or comparison with others.
summary: Self-Righteousness names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. self-righteousness tries to stand before God on personal goodness, religious performance, or comparison with others. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Self-Righteousness because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: self-righteousness tries to stand before God on personal goodness, religious performance, or comparison with others. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because it keeps people near religion while far from grace. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Lay down the need to prove yourself. Come to Christ empty-handed, and teach others that the Gospel is for sinners who need mercy, not performers who need applause. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
